• 1. High: --insecure-http-auth no longer works for device-flow login against non-loopback http:// auth hosts. login still accepts the flag, but it constructs
     the auth client with auth.NewClient(nil) and no way to pass that opt-in through, while the new client hard-codes AllowInsecureHTTP to loopback only
     (cmd/entire/cli/login.go:47, cmd/entire/cli/auth/client.go:50). Before this refactor, the hidden flag disabled the CLI-side HTTPS guard for local/dev auth
     hosts generally; after it, entire login --insecure-http-auth will still fail on something like http://devbox.internal:8787.
  2. Medium: login persists the core token under the raw AuthBaseURL, but the new token manager later looks it up under a normalized issuer. runLogin saves
     with store.SaveToken(client.BaseURL(), token) (cmd/entire/cli/login.go:100), while defaultManager() passes api.AuthBaseURL() into tokenmanager.New, which
     normalizes scheme/host/default port before using it as the store key (cmd/entire/cli/auth/exchange.go:63, cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go:43). That means a
     login done with an equivalent-but-not-canonical issuer such as https://AUTH.example.com:443/ can succeed, but later data-API commands using
     TokenForResource can report “not logged in” because they probe a different keyring entry.
  3. Medium: the new login-time token validation rejects some opaque access tokens even though the comment says opaque tokens are allowed.
     validateReceivedToken only treats tokens.ErrMalformedJWT as “opaque, accept”, but any dotted non-JWT token that fails deeper in ParseClaims becomes a hard
     error via parse claims (cmd/entire/cli/login.go:120). In practice, a 3-segment opaque token or other non-JWT token that happens to look JWT-shaped will
     now fail login unexpectedly.

tokenmanager.New normalises its Issuer config via

it as the tokenstore profile key. Without matching normalisation on the
CLI side, an env value like ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/

hands to tokenmanager as Issuer survives the manager's own normalisation
pass byte-for-byte. AuthBaseURL() applies it; OriginOnly is now an alias
so the search/login call sites that strip arbitrary URLs to origins get
the same canonical form for free.

All three fixes committed cleanly on top of the original series. Final commit graph:

```

```

### What was fixed

**#1 (high): `--insecure-http-auth` regression for non-loopback http auth hosts.** `auth.NewClient` now takes `allowInsecureHTTP bool`, OR'd with `isLoopbackHTTP`. Loopback remains permitted unconditionally; the flag adds non-loopback http on top. login plumbs `insecureHTTPAuth` through. Two regression tests cover the loopback-always-permitted and non-loopback-with-flag cases.

**#2 (medium): keyring key drift from URL normalisation.** Added `api.NormalizeOriginURL` mirroring `oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL` (lowercase scheme/host, strip default port, drop path/query/fragment, collapse trailing slash). `api.AuthBaseURL()` applies it so the value flowing into both `store.SaveToken(api.AuthBaseURL(), ...)` and `tokenmanager.New(Issuer: api.AuthBaseURL())` matches byte-for-byte. `OriginOnly` becomes an alias so the search/login origin-stripping call sites get the same canonical form. Test covers `HTTPS://AUTH.example.com:443/` → `https://auth.example.com`.

**#3 (medium): opaque tokens with JWT-shaped failure modes wrongly rejected.** `validateReceivedToken` now only hard-rejects on `tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT`; any other parse failure (bad base64, bad JSON, bad aud claim, etc.) treats the token as opaque per the doc-comment's promise. Two regression tests cover 3-segment opaque (`aaa.bbb.ccc`) and bad-base64-payload paths.

Verification: `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/auth/... ./cmd/entire/cli/api/... ./cmd/entire/cli/` all pass; `mise run lint` → 0 issues.

### What was fixed

**#1**: `bearerTransport.RoundTrip` now omits the Authorization header when token is empty instead of returning `errEmptyBearerToken` locally. The original concern (no malformed `"Authorization: Bearer "` on the wire) is preserved by simply not setting the header. Regression test in `api/client_test.go` confirms an empty-token request reaches the server with no Authorization header.

**#2**: Added `auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()` setter that flips a package-level `atomic.Bool` read by `defaultManager()` when it builds the tokenmanager. Loopback hosts remain permitted unconditionally; the flag adds non-loopback http on top. The three call sites that own the `--insecure-http-auth` flag (`NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `newRecapClient`, dispatch's `runServer`) invoke the setter before any `TokenForResource` call when the flag is set. Now `entire trail list --insecure-http-auth` against a split-host setup with `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=http://devbox.internal:8787` and `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://api.devbox.internal:9000` actually works end-to-end.

The setter is fire-and-forget — the manager's `AllowInsecureHTTP` freezes on first construction, so callers must opt in before their first token resolution. Tests bypass `exchange.go` entirely via the existing `managerForTest` seam, so the override has no impact on test paths.

gh pr create --title "Integrate auth-go: split-host config + RFC 8693 token exchange" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Migrates the CLI's inline OAuth implementation to the shared `github.com/entireio/auth-go` library, picking up its hardened OAuth client (origin-URL validation, `alg:none` JWT rejection, HTTPS-only with loopback exception, verification_uri validation, centralised error parsing).
- Adds split-host config: `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` for the auth issuer, falling back to `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` so single-host deployments are unchanged. Split-host setups (e.g. `us.auth.partial.to` mints tokens, `partial.to` consumes them) get RFC 8693 token exchange transparently — the data-API bearer is minted on demand from the core token via the auth host's STS endpoint.
- Introduces a provider routing table (`v1`/`v2` via `ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION`) so endpoint paths and the auth-tokens management URL are configured in one place instead of duplicated between `auth/` and `api/`.

## What changed under the hood

**Library integration**
- Pinned `github.com/entireio/auth-go v0.1.1-0.20260520123811-da94c52ef430` (PR #5 head of that repo).
- `auth/client.go` is now a thin shim over `deviceflow.Client`. `auth/store.go` implements `tokenstore.Store`. `auth/exchange.go` wires a package-level `tokenmanager.Manager` and exposes `TokenForResource(ctx, url)` / `Token(ctx, req)`.
- All eight data-API callers (activity, dispatch_wizard, recap, search completion, trail ×4, watch) now thread `cmd.Context()` and obtain bearers via `auth.TokenForResource`. Dispatch's cloud mode and recap join the same path.

**Security hardening**
- Login validates the received token before persisting: rejects `alg:none` JWTs (`tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT`), enforces `iss` matches the configured issuer, refuses pre-expired tokens. Opaque (non-JWT) tokens are accepted unconditionally — every parse failure other than `ErrUnsignedJWT` is treated as opaque per the doc-comment promise.
- `api.AuthBaseURL()` canonicalises to match `tokenmanager`'s internal normalisation (lowercase scheme/host, strip default port, drop path/query/fragment), so the keyring key login wrote matches the one the manager later reads byte-for-byte.
- `bearerTransport` omits the Authorization header when the bearer is empty rather than sending a malformed `"Authorization: Bearer "`. This preserves recap's "let the server return a typed 401" UX without exposing a malformed header.
- `--insecure-http-auth` is threaded through both the deviceflow client (`auth.NewClient(httpClient, allowInsecureHTTP)`) and the tokenmanager (`auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()` setter), so split-host local-dev on plain HTTP works end-to-end. Loopback hosts remain permitted unconditionally either way.

**Code quality**
- New `api.OriginOnly` / `api.NormalizeOriginURL` helpers replace what would have been three copy-paste sites for stripping URLs to their origin (in `search_cmd.go`'s search-host resolution, `login.go`'s `iss` comparison, and `api.AuthBaseURL`).
- `newAuthHostAPIClient(token)` deduplicates the auth-token management endpoint construction across status/list/revoke/logout.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues.
- [x] `mise run test` — 5294 unit tests pass, 3 skipped.
- [x] `mise run test:integration` — 348 integration tests pass.
- [x] `mise run test:ci` — full CI (unit + integration + Vogon canary) exit 0.
- [ ] **Manual:** verify split-host deployment against the partial.to staging environment (`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://us.auth.partial.to`, `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to`) — `entire login`, `entire trail list`, `entire dispatch` should all exchange through the STS endpoint.
- [ ] **Manual:** verify `entire login --insecure-http-auth` against a non-loopback http auth host (e.g. `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=http://devbox.internal:8787`) — previously failed with `ErrInsecureBaseURL`; should now complete.
- [ ] **Manual:** verify `entire recap` when logged out — the request should reach the server (no `Authorization` header) and recap should render its "sign in" message rather than a transport error.
- [ ] **Manual:** verify `entire login` with a non-canonical issuer (`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/`) — the saved keyring entry should be readable by subsequent `entire trail list` / `entire status` etc. (no spurious "not logged in").

## Related work

- Reference: this is a fresh implementation of [#1153](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1153)'s integration on top of [auth-go PR #5](https://github.com/entireio/auth-go/pull/5)'s hardening. Once auth-go PR #5 ships as v0.2.0, the `go.mod` pseudo-version should bump to the released tag.

=== cmd/entire/cli/auth/client_test.go:81 ===
`TestSecondsUntil_FutureExpiry` mutates the package-level `nowFunc` but is marked `t.Parallel()`. This can race with other parallel tests in the same package (e.g. `TestSecondsUntil_ZeroExpiry`) and make the suite flaky. Consider removing `t.Parallel()` for this test (or avoid global mutation by passing a clock into `secondsUntil`).


=== cmd/entire/cli/auth/client.go:175 ===
`secondsUntil` can return a negative value if `ExpiresAt` is in the past (clock skew, scheduling delays, or tests overriding `nowFunc`). Historically `ExpiresIn` was non-negative; clamping at 0 (e.g. `max(0, ...)`) would avoid surprising negative durations leaking into callers/logging.



=== cmd/entire/cli/api_client.go:42 ===
`auth.TokenForResource` expects an origin-style URL (scheme+host, no path/query). `api.BaseURL()` is only trimmed for trailing slashes and can still include a path if a user sets `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` that way. To avoid token resolution failures in that configuration, consider passing `api.OriginOnly(dataURL)` (and using the same origin-only value for the token request).


=== cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/mode_cloud.go:37 ===
`lookupResourceToken`/`auth.TokenForResource` is passed `baseURL := api.BaseURL()`, which may include a path if `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` is configured that way. Since token exchange typically requires an origin-only resource (scheme+host), consider using `api.OriginOnly(baseURL)` when resolving the token to prevent invalid-resource errors for path-bearing base URLs.

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Address Copilot review: strip path from TokenForResource resources, clamp secondsUntil

Three call sites — NewAuthenticatedAPIClient, newRecapClient, and
dispatch's runServer — fed raw api.BaseURL() into auth.TokenForResource.
tokenmanager validates Resource as a strict origin URL, so a deployment
with ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1 (path-bearing) would
fail token resolution before any request was sent. api.OriginOnly()
strips the path; search_cmd.go already did this, so the three other
sites now match.

secondsUntil could return a negative integer when ExpiresAt was already
in the past (clock skew, scheduling delay, tests overriding nowFunc to
a future time then querying an already-elapsed expiry). Historically
the deviceflow polling response carried a non-negative expires_in;
downstream loggers and any code displaying remaining lifetime didn't
expect a negative value. max(0, ...) clamps the result and a new
regression test covers the past-expiry path.

TestSecondsUntil_FutureExpiry mutates the package-level nowFunc under
t.Parallel(), which races any other parallel test (including the new
TestSecondsUntil_PastExpiryClampsToZero) that also reads it. Dropping
t.Parallel() on both tests is the minimum fix — a deeper refactor would
take a clock parameter, but the call-site is internal-only and the
mutation is bounded by t.Cleanup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

      - name: Run golangci-lint

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Align CI Go version with auth-go's 1.26.3 requirement

CI's lint workflow uses actions/setup-go with go-version: 'stable',
which currently resolves to Go 1.26.2 on GitHub-hosted runners. The
auth-go dep transitively raised our go.mod minimum to 1.26.3, so
golangci-lint fails on PR runs with:

  go.mod requires go >= 1.26.3 (running go 1.26.2; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)

Two changes keep CI in sync:

  - mise.toml: bump the mise-managed Go to 1.26.3 so every workflow
    that uses mise-action (test-core, test-integration, e2e canary,
    etc.) picks up the right version.
  - .github/workflows/lint.yml: switch setup-go from 'stable' to
    go-version-file: go.mod. This matches release.yml's pattern and
    makes the lint job auto-track go.mod going forward, so the next
    Go bump doesn't need a parallel workflow edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

CI is green — `lint` passes (2m41s), all test shards pass, CodeQL/binary-size/licenses all pass.

### Summary

Two follow-up commits pushed:

**`b000b76fb` — Address Copilot review**
- `api.OriginOnly()` now strips path from `BaseURL()` at the three remaining `TokenForResource` call sites (`api_client.go`, `recap.go`, `dispatch/mode_cloud.go`). Tokenmanager validates Resource as origin-only — a path-bearing `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` would have failed token resolution before any request.
- `secondsUntil` now clamps to 0 via `max(0, ...)` so clock skew can't surface a negative value to downstream loggers.
- Dropped `t.Parallel()` from `TestSecondsUntil_FutureExpiry` (and the new `TestSecondsUntil_PastExpiryClampsToZero`) — both mutate the package-level `nowFunc`, which would race other parallel tests in the package.

**`c77c63dfd` — Align CI Go version**
- `mise.toml`: bumped pinned Go from 1.26.2 → 1.26.3 to match the go.mod minimum imposed transitively by auth-go.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml`: switched `setup-go` from `go-version: 'stable'` to `go-version-file: go.mod` — matches `release.yml`'s pattern and auto-tracks future bumps.

Replied to all four inline Copilot comments pointing at the fix commit. PR #1239's checks are now green.

message.content: Should we do afresh PR just updating go first?

content.text:
Yes — good instinct. Bumping `mise.toml` from Go 1.26.2 → 1.26.3 affects every workflow that uses mise-action (test-core, integration shards, e2e canary, etc.), not just lint. Isolating it has two wins:

1. **Smaller blast radius**: if the Go bump surfaces issues elsewhere, it's clearly the bump, not the auth-go work.
2. **Trivial review**: a 4-line diff (Go pin + workflow file) is a 30-second review for whoever lands it.

The downside is just managing a second PR. Worth it.

**Proposed plan:**
1. Branch off `origin/main` with just `mise.toml` + `.github/workflows/lint.yml` from `c77c63dfd`.
2. Open that as a small PR ("Bump Go to 1.26.3 for upcoming auth-go dep" or similar).
3. Once it lands, rebase `soph/auth-go` onto the new main and drop `c77c63dfd` — its content will already be there.

Want me to do that now? I'd just need to:
- `git checkout -b soph/bump-go-1.26.3 origin/main`
- Cherry-pick `c77c63dfd` (or just re-apply the two-file change)
- Push and `gh pr create`

And then later rebase `soph/auth-go` once the small PR merges.

- Bumping `go.mod` from `go 1.26.2` → `go 1.26.3`.
- Dropping the "(required by auth-go)" reference from the lint.yml comment per your direction; the comment now just notes the auto-tracking benefit.

Replied to all three inline comments. PR is ready to land — once it does I'll rebase #1239 and drop its now-redundant CI-alignment commit.
